translation.title: Diclofenac Sodium Plaster
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for osteoarthritis, periarthritis of the shoulder, tendinitis and tenosynovitis, peritendinitis, elbow pain (tennis elbow, etc.), muscle pain, and post-traumatic swelling and pain.
translation.usage: Apply 1 plaster to the affected area 1 to 2 times a day.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, if you have experienced hypersensitivity or asthma caused by aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, if you are a child under 18, a pregnant woman past the fifth month of pregnancy, breastfeeding, or a patient with peptic ulcer. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if you have bronchial asthma, if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, or elderly. Do not use continuously for more than 7 days. Do not apply to skin with lesions (exudative dermatitis, eczema, infected lesions, burns, wounds, etc.), or to the eyes or mucous membranes. Do not use an occlusive dressing without a doctor's supervision. Do not use together with other diclofenac products or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before using together with new-quinolone antibacterials (enoxacin, etc.); convulsions may occur. Photosensitivity reactions, swelling, skin peeling, eczema, dry skin, sometimes dermatitis, itching, redness, roughness, or irritation, rarely blistering or pigmentation, and at the application site redness, red spots, rash, itching, pain, swelling, blisters, erosion, hypersensitivity reactions, angioneurotic edema, or asthma may occur. If any of these occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Store at room temperature away from moisture and light, and keep out of reach of children.
